back: Eligible must be activated and leaves no privilege at rest. Active is standing privilege. Keyword: nothing held at rest.

front: Key Vault access policy vs RBAC
back: Access policies grant operations on the whole vault. RBAC scopes to an individual secret and is the recommended model. Keyword: per-secret scope.
Prevents even a privileged user permanently destroying a vault or its contents before retention expires. Soft delete alone does not. Keyword: cannot be purged.
Finds credentials that were never put in a vault — in a VM disk, a container image, or code. Keyword: secrets outside the vault.
Contributor manages resources but cannot grant access. User Access Administrator grants access but cannot manage resources. Keyword: split on purpose.
A custom role can only be assigned within the scopes listed in its assignableScopes. Keyword: where it may be used.
Created only by Azure-managed services such as blueprints and managed applications, never by an administrator directly. Keyword: not authorable.
Remediating effects require a managed identity with enough rights to perform the remediation. Keyword: no identity, no remediation.
Brings existing resources into line, because DeployIfNotExists only fires on create or update by itself. Keyword: existing resources need a push.
CanNotDelete and ReadOnly apply regardless of role — an Owner is stopped until they remove the lock. Keyword: outranks RBAC.
A group of policies assigned as one object; the regulatory compliance dashboard is built on them. Keyword: standard as one unit.
A resource guard requires a second, separately privileged approver before destructive backup operations. Keyword: two people.
Managed identity, then federated credential, then certificate, and a client secret only when nothing else works. Keyword: least stored.
Forces every storage request through Microsoft Entra authorisation. The account key grants everything and is attributable to nobody. Keyword: no shared key.
Signed with Entra credentials, so it is revocable and attributable, unlike an account SAS signed with the account key. Keyword: revocable.
Service endpoint still reaches the public endpoint and keeps a public IP. Private endpoint projects the resource into the VNet as a private IP. Keyword: private IP.
The public host name must resolve to the private IP via a linked private DNS zone. Reachable by IP but not by name means DNS. Keyword: DNS is the usual fault.
Allowing an inbound flow implicitly permits its return traffic. A matching outbound rule is unnecessary. Keyword: return traffic is implicit.
Lets a rule name a logical group of NICs instead of an address range, so it stays correct as machines are added. Keyword: name, not address.

front: Virtual Network Manager security admin rules
back: Evaluated before NSGs and cannot be overridden by a subscription owner's own NSG. Keyword: platform team wins.
DNAT rules, then network rules, then application rules. Application rules are the FQDN filters. Keyword: DNAT first.
Adds TLS inspection, IDPS, and URL filtering over the Standard tier. Keyword: inspect inside TLS.
A Virtual WAN hub with Azure Firewall deployed into it; routing intent then forces traffic through that inspection point. Keyword: inspection in the hub.
Keys stay with the client, so even a database administrator sees ciphertext. The answer for privileged insiders. Keyword: DBA cannot read it.
Obscures results for unprivileged users. A presentation control, not encryption — the data is unchanged. Keyword: not encryption.

front: SQL vulnerability assessment vs threat protection
back: Assessment scans configuration against a baseline. Threat protection alerts on injection and anomalous access. Keyword: state vs event.
The Network Watcher diagnostic that answers why a specific flow was allowed or dropped. Keyword: why did it drop.
An assistant answers within existing permissions, so over-shared but undiscovered content becomes reachable on request. Keyword: permissions become discoverable.
Gives an agent a first-class identity so Conditional Access applies and access can be managed and revoked. Keyword: agents are identities.
Defender XDR shows what a compromised agent could reach, not merely what it did. Keyword: could, not did.
Fronts Foundry with token limits, rate limiting, and centralised key handling. Keyword: token budget.
Browser-based RDP and SSH over TLS, so no VM needs a public IP and no management port is exposed. Keyword: no public IP.
Management port stays closed and is opened for a requested source and duration after approval. Keyword: minutes, not permanent.
Secure boot plus vTPM, with integrity monitoring attesting that boot was not tampered with. Keyword: attested boot.
Encrypts memory so the host itself cannot read it. Keyword: host cannot read memory.
Projects on-premises and other-cloud servers into Azure as resources so Defender, Policy, and machine configuration reach them. Keyword: extend Azure outward.

front: Defender for Servers Plan 1 vs Plan 2
back: Plan 1 is EDR only. Plan 2 adds vulnerability assessment, file integrity monitoring, JIT, and agentless scanning. Keyword: FIM or JIT means Plan 2.
Snapshots the disk and analyses it out of band — coverage without installing anything, traded against real-time detection. Keyword: no agent, no real time.
A shared credential that should stay disabled; use Entra authentication with the AcrPull role instead. Keyword: disable the admin account.
Run in detection mode to find false positives, then switch to prevention. Straight to prevention breaks the app. Keyword: detect first.
Chains findings into a route an attacker could actually take and prioritises by the chain rather than by individual severity. Keyword: the route, not the finding.
Foundational is free recommendations and secure score. Defender CSPM adds attack paths, security explorer, agentless and secret scanning. Keyword: paid adds the graph.
Discovers internet-facing assets from outside, including ones the organisation does not know it owns. Keyword: outside-in.
Packages connectors, analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks for a product — the expected way to onboard a source. Keyword: onboard as a package.
Analytics is queryable and alertable; basic and auxiliary are cheap but restricted; archive is long retention with search jobs. Keyword: cheap logs cannot alert.
Choose which Windows Security event set is gathered — the main Sentinel cost control. Keyword: collect less.
Automation rules do lightweight in-Sentinel actions and control ordering. Playbooks are Logic Apps that do the real work. Keyword: triage vs act.
A playbook acts through a managed identity that must hold the necessary roles. Keyword: grant the identity.
The provisioned capacity Security Copilot runs on, and the thing that is billed. Keyword: capacity, not licences.
It answers from what its enabled plugins can reach; a disabled plugin yields a confident answer built on nothing. Keyword: no plugin, no data.
